name: Sea Blue
lede: Sea blue is a medium blue with a green cast, the color of open water as a plain-language name.

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body:
The books use sea blue as an ordinary description rather than a defined term. Finlay lists it among the bales and samples of cloth in a weaving loom shed, next to coral and mist [1].

Birren reports that ancient astrologers gave each zodiac sign a color, with sea-blue for Pisces [2]. Birren's 1950 book is old opinion rather than modern evidence, so read the list as a historical curiosity [2]. A study of early abstract painting also has a numbered color list that includes a sea-blue [3]. The phrase works as a plain-language name: it points at no dye, mineral or maker, only at the sea [1][2]. None of the three sources gives it a recipe or a fixed shade, so the swatch below is a modern reading of the name, not a historical match [1][2][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #047495 is a clear blue-teal, less green than [[teal]] and darker than [[azure]] [4]. It is close to [[marine-blue]] and [[steel-blue]] [4]. Screen colors are approximate [4].
